lawyer:
Dr. Kamal Hossain with HS Deb Brahman and Tanjibul-Alam, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
AJ Mohammad Ali, Additional Attorney-General with Naima Haider, Deputy Attorney-General and MA Azim Khair, Deputy Attorney-General and Md Alamgir Kabir; Assistant Attorney-General ----- For Respondent No. 1. 
Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed with MK Rahman, Md Mohsin Rashid, Advocates ----- For Added Respondent No.8.
parties:
Engineer Mahmudul Islam and others ----- Petitioners 
Vs
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman, J: Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause why the impugned memo dated 28-4-1998 containing the approval of the project issued by the respondent No. 4 (Annexure J to the writ petition) pursuant to government approval dated 25-3-1998, minutes of the meeting of the Co-ordination Committee dated 16-6-1998 (Annexure K to the writ petition and Memo dated 18-6-1998 (Annexure L to the writ petition) and the actions taken pursuant thereto should not be declared to have been made arbitrarily, are unconstitutional, without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 3. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule are that, the impugned approval for setting up of container terminals given by the government in favour of the respondent No. 8 communicated vides Memo No. MOS/8-/Chi-1/98- 96 dated 28-4-1998, (evidenced by Annexure J to the writ petition) has been challenged by the petitioners contending, amongst others, that the approval has been given arbitrarily, without application of mind, unreasonably and against public interest inasmuch as the proposed container terminals if established will destroy the existence and functioning of the existing Chittagong Port and that the approval has been given without evaluating the past record of the respondent No. 8 as to its capability of performance, financial soundness and in the absence of the project feasibility report and that the approval has been given on an application submitted on 29-12-1997 in the name of the respondent No. 8 Company, claiming to be an affiliate of Stevedoring Services of America, an USA-based Company, and without considering the applications of other applicants who applied for establishment of such container terminals at the relevant time and without inviting international tender to and that as per provisions of the Chittagong Port Authority Ordinance 1976 (CPA Ordinance) the approval as given is beyond jurisdiction, since Chittagong Port Authority, being authorised to give such permission, has not been consulted prior to granting the impugned approval; and that there was non-application of mind on the part of the government executives as contemplated under the Rules of Business framed under Article 55 of the Constitution for proper exercise of executive authority, who failed to (a) consider identification of the priority of the project; (b) consider the commercial feasibility of the project, since not furnished; (c) assess the financial capability of the respondent No.8; (d) the necessity for publication of advertisement inviting competitive bids to get best offer and thus the provisions of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution have been violated; and that the persons involved in processing the proposal of respondent No. 8 failed to consider the decision of the Ministry of Shipping taken on 11-7-1995 for setting up of container terminals outside the Port area by invitation of offers through notifications, to be made by the Chittagong Port Authority (evidenced by Annexure Z-3 to the affidavit in reply); and that the impugned approval has been given without considering and not following the Guidelines suggested for Private Sector Participation in Ports, 1997 (evidenced by Annexure F to the writ petition) and without collecting the information as recommended in the report submitted to the World Bank in respect of the Port Privatisation and Development Project for Container Terminals at Patenga, Chittagong (evidenced by Annexure Z-4 to the affidavit in-reply to the affidavit in opposition filed by the respondent No. 8) and that the government acted discriminatorily in not considering the proposals submitted during the relevant period, apart from the proposals submitted subsequently; and that the Board of Investment (BOI) also acted arbitrarily and without application of mind in giving registration to the proposed project of the respondent No.8. 

 4. The respondent No.1 and the respondent No. 8 contested the Rule by filing affidavits-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits thereto separately. The contents of the affidavits-in- opposition of both the respondent Nos. 1 and 8, more or less, are similar. Both the respondents have raised objection as to the locus standi of the petitioners and the maintainability of the writ petition. They asserted that the subject matter of the writ petition relates to the policy of the government, hence in the absence of arbitrariness, such action is not amenable to the writ jurisdiction of this Court and that the government has acted in accordance with law in giving the impugned approval and that the Master Plan of CPA dated 15-5-1995 provides for establishment of container terminals at Patenga by private sector on BOO basis and that the parties, who submitted proposals, failed to submit formal proposals at the relevant time, and that the respondent No. 8 submitted its proposal dated 29-12-1997 to the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping, and the same was duly processed and that the Ministry of Shipping received a complete proposal from the respondent No. 8 in two(2) volumes, one volume under the caption "SSA Bangladesh Limited" and the other volume under the caption "Business Plan, December, 1997" containing feasibility report, guidelines and all other documents along with the application dated 29-12-1997 and that by a letter dated 14-1-1998 the Board of Investment communicated to the respondent No. 8 the news about granting its registration, copy of which was also endorsed to the respondent Nos. 1 and 7; and that as per Rules of Business the summary on the project-proposal of respondent No.8 was sent to the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 2-2-1998 for decision, who in turn ordered for scrutiny of the proposal by the Council Committee on Economic Affairs and the said Council Committee in its meeting held on 25-3-1998 throughly examined and evaluated the proposal of respondent No.8 and recommended for approval by the Hon'ble Prime Minister and thereafter, on approval by the Hon'ble Prime Minister the Cabinet Division vide letter 26-4-1998 communicated the decision to the Ministry of Shipping, and the Ministry accordingly, on 28-4-1998, issued the impugned letter of approval to the respondent No.8; and that in the Industrial Policy of 1991, the Port sector has been kept open for private sector investment and that the establishment of container terminal at Patenga under the private sector on BOO basis is also included in the Master Plan of Chittagong Port for the years 1995 to 2010 AD and that in the meeting held on 13-6-1995 under the Chairmanship of the then Shipping Minister, Mr. MK Anwar, (Annexure 11 to the affidavit-in-opposition of respondent No.1) it was resolved that setting up of new container terminal under private sector outside the protected Port area would be welcomed; and that the approval given in favour of the respondent No.8 is not an exclusive permission and if any other company is interested to establish such project may apply accordingly, the Board of Investment may approve the same and that as per Rules of Business the Council Committee on Economic Affairs is authorised to approve or recommend for approval of such private foreign investment project; and that the Government of Bangladesh is not at any risk in approving the project since it will not require to make any investment or provide any State guarantee or commercial risk guarantee and hence the question of competitive bid is not relevant in the instant project, which is open and non-exclusive in nature and more terminals may be permitted to be set up, and that in the meeting of the Parliamentary Standing Committee of the Ministry of Shipping held on 1-3-1999 the issue was discussed but no recommendation has been made and that since 1998 the government has carried out either directly or through Chittagong Port Authority nine(9) studies with financial assistance of World Bank or ADB in the greater interest of the nation, specifically to facilitate smooth import and export through setting up of private container terminals and the same will be beneficial for the country and that with the implementation of proposed project additional job facility will be created. It is further stated in the affidavits filed by the respondent Nos. 1 and 8 that the government is not required to provide any fund, asset and or to share any natural resource with the respondent No. 8 and hence competitive bid is not relevant in this project and that the establishment of private container terminals by the private sector is open to all and the permission given in favour of the respondent. No. 8 is not exclusive and any private party at any time can apply for permission to establish more private container terminals for which there is no restriction and that the approval in reference has been given under the authority vested with the government under the Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1980 and in terms of the Board of Investment Board Act, 1989 and as per Industrial Policy, 1991 (as revised); and that the respondent No.8 company is a Joint Venture Company, in which Orient Maritime Limited (a Bangladeshi Company) and SSA Netherlands BV of Netherlands (subsidiary of Stevedoring Services of America of USA), are the only two(2) shareholders; and that after the approval and registration of the project by the Board of Investment the Ministry of Shipping as per Rules of Business processed the application of the respondent No.8 and after issuance of the impugned letter of approval the Ministry of Shipping constituted a Co-ordination Committee to facilitate the implementation of the project and the said Committee in its meeting dated 6-8-1998 recommended for issuance of letter to the concerned Ministry and Agencies for allotment of required lands and for requisition of further lands in favour of the respondent No. 8 for the project and that accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, initiated land acquisition proceeding and required the respondent 8 to deposit Taka 30,47,46,883.94 as compensation money for acquisition of lands, and that memorandum of understanding has been signed for taking on lease certain lands belonging to Bangladesh Water Development Board; and that the Ministry of Shipping is examining further if more advantage from the foreign investors can be negotiated and accordingly, a committee with senior officials has been formed and that in between 21-5-2000 and 26-1-2000 the said committee of five(5) Secretaries, appointed on 14-5-1998, held 74 meetings with the respondent No. 8 and other experts on the draft Agreement for Implementation prepared by respondent No. 8 and the end result is the draft implementation agreement dated 5-3-2001, which was subsequently sent to the Ministry of Law for vetting and on receipt therefrom after vetting, the Ministry of Shipping sent the said draft implementation agreement dated 5-3-2001 to the Committee of five(5) Secretaries and that thereafter the said 5 members committee was reconstituted with the six(6) Secretaries, which held 7 meetings in between 2-3-2002 and 30-4-2002 and submitted its report to the Cabinet Division with its recommendations dated 30-4-2002 and that a summary dated 4-5-2002 was then placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minister for approval of a proposal for constituting. A negotiating committee with the aforesaid 6 Secretaries for getting further benefits for the country and on 14-5-2002, after obtaining approval of the Hon'ble Prime Minister, the negotiating committee was formed and the said committee held meetings from 18-5-2002 to 25-5-2002 with the respondent No. 8 and in the said meetings IIFC rendered its expert assistance and it has been agreed that the project will be completed under BOT basis in place of approved BOO basis and after 30 years the ownership with all assets will vest in the government and thus the original approval has been amended and that as the matter involves national interest the terms and conditions of the implementation agreement is being further scrutinised and is yet to be finalised and that the sane will go through the following stages: 

 (c) Submitting the agreement in its final shape with a summary to the Council Committee on Economic Affairs for deliberation and recommendation for the approval of Hon'ble Prime Minister; 

 (d) Forwarding the recommendation of the Council Committee on Economic Affairs along with a summary to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for approval, and 

 5. The respondent No.8 apart from aforesaid statements made in their affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits, annexed papers and documents which includes consent letter for establishment of the project from the Chittagong Development Authority (evidenced by Annexure XXX of the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 8 dated 17-6-2002), the English version of the recommendations made by the Committee of 6 Secretaries in their report dated 30-4-2002, (at pages 27 to 30 of the Supplementary Affidavit of respondent No.8 dated 17-7-2002), the summary containing the recommendation sent to the Hon'ble Prime Minister dated 4-5-2002 (at pages 31 to 40 of the Supplementary Affidavit of respondent No.8 dated 17-7-2002) and the approval thereof by the Hon'ble Prime Minister dated 6-5-2002 and the copy of the notification dated 14-5-2002 authorising the committee of six (6) Secretaries to negotiate with respondent No.8. 

 7. Dr. Kamal Hossain, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submitted that the impugned approval has been given arbitrarily, without application of mind, without relying on reasonableness and against public interest and that the officials involved in the process of giving approval to the proposal of the respondent No.8 are guilty of culpable negligence. In elaborating his submissions the learned Advocate, referring to the application of the respondent No.8 for approval of the project dated 29-12-1997 (Annexure I to the writ petition, copy of which is also annexed as Annexure VIII to the affidavit-in-opposition dated 17-6-2002 of the respondent No.8) submitted that the respondent No.8 described itself as an Affiliate of Stevedoring Services of America, USA, and in the letter dated 29-12-1997 it is mentioned that the "Stevedoring Service of America (SSA) of the USA and Orient Maritime Ltd of Bangladesh formed the joint venture company with intention to Build, Own and Operate (BOO) the proposed container terminal Ports at Pangaon, Dhaka and at Patenga in Chittagong." Then referring to the summary dated 2-2-1998 placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minister (Annexures 3 to the affidavit-in-opposition dated 15-11-2002 of the respondent No.1) it has been submitted that therein it has been disclosed that the respondent No. 8 is a Joint Venture Company, consists of USA and Bangladeshi Companies, but the papers and documents available to the officers and persons concerned, who initiated the notes in the file and prepared the summary for the Hon'ble Prime Minister, show that the respondent No. 8 company has been registered in Bangladesh as a Joint Venture private limited company with 2 shareholders, who are corporate bodies, of which one is a Bangladeshi Company and other is a Netherlands Company, In support of his contention that the foreigner share-holder is a Netherlands company, the learned Advocate referred to the Articles of Association of respondent No. 8 company, copy of which has been annexed as Annexure H 1 to the writ petition, wherein it has been clearly mentioned that "SSA Netherlands" is also known as SSA Netherland BV, is a Netherlands Company and thus the notes and summary have been made and prepared with incorrect description of the respondent No.8, as to the nationality of its constituents and that the approval, in fact, has been given in favour of a USA-Bangladesh join venture company, not in existence. The officials concerned in initiating the notes for impugned approval of the project proposal of respondent No. 8 have acted negligently, arbitrarily and without basis and further they initiated the notes in the file in the absence of any financial analysis or feasibility report in respect of the project and that no man of prudence will proceed to consider any proposal of any project without examining "feasibility and or financial report" for primary satisfaction as to the viability of such project, and particularly in respect of a national project of this nature. The learned Advocate then submitted that when the proposal of the respondent No. 8 was being considered there were also other applications, but those were not considered properly and in support of his contention the learned Advocate referred to Annexure G to the writ petition, a proposal dated 3rd March, 1997 made by a British Company namely, Overseas Trade Service; Annexure M to writ petition, a proposal dated 4-1-1999 of Port Joint Venture Ltd (which is appears to be a British Company), Annexure N to the writ .petition a proposal dated 1-1-1998 of PSA Corporation Ltd a Singapore company, Annexure Z-17 a proposal dated 20-2-1998 by P & O Australia Ports PTY Ltd and Annexure Z -18 dated 15-8-1997by Asia Containers Services Ltd of Newark. The learned Advocate also referred to Annexures Z-6 dated 7-4-1997, Z-7 dated 1-5-1997, Z-8 dated 3-3-1998 and Z-10 dated 23-9-1998 to show that the Overseas Trade Service was pursuing the government with its proposal. Referring to Annexure Z-9, copy of the letter dated 2-9-1998 addressed to the Hon'ble Prime Minister, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that the Port Joint Venture Ltd has shown its interest for a Joint Venture for establishment of a container terminal at Chittagong. It has been submitted on behalf of the petitioners that although in the initial letter of proposal dated 29-12-1997 of the respondent No.8 and in the summary dated 2-2-1998 placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minister, it has been categorically mentioned that the respondent No. 8 company is a Joint Venture Company of USA and Bangladeshi share-holders but the Articles of Association of the respondent No. 8 company (Annexure H-1) confirms that the Company was not incorporated as a Joint Venture Company of USA and Bangladesh -but is a joint venture company of Bangladesh and Netherlands; and that the impugned approval, as it appears, was given in favour of a USA-Bangladesh joint venture company and thus the impugned approval has been procured through fraud by misleading the recommending and approving authorities disclosing false identity of the foreign share-holder of the respondent No.8 Company and this proves that the impugned approval is the result of negligence and non-application of mind on the part of the officers in not examining and not considering the status as well as the nationality of the shareholders of the respondent No.8 company. The learned Advocate then referring to the report dated 30-4-2002 of the Committee of 6 Secretaries and the statements made in the affidavits-in- opposition of the respondent Nos. 1 and 8 submitted that it is incorrect to say that at the relevant time i.e. prior to 28-4-1998, the government did not receive any application from any foreign party showing interest for setting up of container terminals at Patenga and hence the government had no alternative but to consider the unsolicited offer of the respondent No. 8 and in support of his contention the learned Advocate again referred to Annexure G to the writ petition, Annexures Z-6, Z- 7, Z-8, Z-17 and Z-18 of the affidavit-in-reply dated 30-7-2002 of the writ petitioners, which are letters of Overseas Trade Services dated 1-5-1997 to the Minister for Shipping, dated 3-3-1998 to the Executive Chairman, Board of Investment, and a letter dated 20-2-1998 of Ms. P&O Ports Australia and letter dated 15-8-1997 of Asia Container Terminal Services Ltd showing their respective interest for setting up of Container Terminal Ports in Bangladesh. The learned Advocate referring to Annexure Z-10 to the affidavit-in-reply of the writ petitioners dated 30-7-2002 submitted that the Joint Chief of Ministry of Shipping by his letter dated 23- 9-1998, in reply to the letter of the Overseas Trade Services, disclosed that the government has already approved a proposal of USA Joint Venture Company and therefore it is incorrect to say that the government was not aware of any other party which has shown any interest to the Authority for setting up of container terminals at the time when the process of the impugned approval was going on. Thus the action of the executives in processing the project proposal of respondent No. 8 without inviting competitive bid for setting up of the Container Terminals is arbitrary and discriminatory. The learned Advocate referring paragraph Nos. 3.2, 3.3, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.3.3, 3.4, and 3.6, as appearing at pages 25, 26 and 27 [a portion of the report of the Committee of six(6) Secretaries dated 30-4-2002] of the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 1 dated 22-7-2002) and paragraph 10 of the summary dated 4-5-2002 prepared for Hon'ble Prime Minister (appearing at page 39 of the supplementary affidavit of the respondent No. 8 dated 17-7-2002) submitted that the committee was trying to justify the impugned approval given to the respondent No.8, admitting that it would have been better if such approval could be given after inviting competitive bids through advertisement, which could bring better proposal for the country, on the plea of "delay". However the Committee of six (6) Secretaries also mentioned in the report that if the impugned approval is not sustained then there may be legal complications and that the country would be much benefited since the country is not required to invest any money in the proposed project. The learned Advocate also submitted that the officials and persons concerned in processing and approving the proposal of the respondent No.8, either failed to consider that by asking for competitive bid more beneficial proposal could be available or they were favoring a private party against the public interest unreasonably and unfairly. The learned Advocate continued to submit that such actions of the government officials involved in the process of approval of the proposal tantamount to culpable negligence and are arbitrary and discriminatory. 

 8. Referring to the process of the incorporation of the respondent No.8 company by the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies of Bangladesh, the learned Advocate submitted that this Court has already been pleased to hold that the respondent No.8 company has been incorporated illegally, as at the time of incorporation of the company, the materials on record shows that there were two (2) share-holders of which one is a Bangladeshi Company and the other is a Netherlands Company but it has been found that the Netherlands Company was not in existence at the time of incorporation of the respondent No. 8 company and therefore the incorporation of respondent No. 8 as a company with only one legal share holder namely, Orient Maritime Ltd, under the Companies Act 1994 was illegal. A company with only one share holder cannot exist in the eye of law and a contract with an illegal company is void ab initio. Therefore the impugned approval given in favour of the illegally incorporated respondent No. 8 company is void ab initio. 

 9. The learned Advocate then submitted that the petitioners did not and have no occasion to challenge any agreement and or the terms and conditions of the proposed agreement of implementation in reference but have challenged the impugned approval, which till date stands as it was. In elaborating his submissions the learned Advocate submitted that although there were discussions and negotiations for changes in and amendments to the terms and conditions of proposed "agreement for implementation" but no agreement till today has been executed or is in existence. The learned Advocate contended that there are 2 draft agreements one dated 5-3-2001 and the other 22-5-2002. The draft agreement dated 25-5-2002 is the amended and modified version of the draft agreement dated 5-3-2001 with beneficial terms in favour of Bangladesh which shows that the committee of five(5) Secretaries failed to act fairly and reasonably and the committee of six(6) Secretaries have rescued the interest of the country or alternatively the committee of five (5) Secretaries acted against the public interest and unfairly, since was eager to enter into the proposed agreement for implementation at an early date. 

 10. The learned Advocate submitted that the petitioners did not challenge the terms and conditions of the Agreement for Implementation under process or any agreement but challenged the process of the impugned approval contained in the letter dated 28-4-1998 and therefore the application as made is not a premature one. The learned Advocate referring to the observations and decision given in the case of Ekushe Television Ltd and others vs Dr. Chowdhury Mahmood Hasan and others [reported in 2002 BLD (AD) 163] submitted that the petitioners have locus standi to file the writ petition and the application is also maintainable inasmuch as the officials involved in the process of the impugned approval have acted arbitrarily and against public interest to give advantage to a private party. It has been further submitted that in view of the disclosures made by the contesting respondents that the major change in the basic structure of the scheme has been agreed upon by the contesting respondents which is as per impugned approval the project was to be implemented under BOO (Build Operate and Own) basis and now agreed to be implemented under BOT (Built, Operate Transfer) basis and such subsequent change of the proposal of the respondent No. 8 being beneficial for the country is sufficient for maintaining the writ petition. It has been submitted that the question of locus standi is not a question of jurisdiction but question of exercise of discretion by the Court on due consideration of the facts and circumstances of each case. Under the Constitution State executives are duty bound to act in accordance with the law with reasonableness and not against the public interest but in the instant case it is seen that the State executives involved in the process of the impugned approval have acted unreasonably without proper application of mind, arbitrarily, without giving due consideration to the public interest and for the interest of a private party inasmuch as though at the relevant period more than one foreign company had shown interest for the similar project yet without calling for a competitive bid, the impugned approval was given, that too in the absence of any formal detailed project profile with financial analysis as to the loss and profit in the business of the project and the expected total annual income from the project and, for that matter, income of the Government of Bangladesh and that a project proposal, without viability report without a financial analysis as to profit and loss accounts of the project, cannot merit consideration and hence the impugned approval is without lawful authority and is liable to be struck down. 

 11. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Additional Attorney-General, appearing for the respondent No.1, submitted that the issue involved in the writ petition is premature one inasmuch as the government is still in the process of finalising the project contract. The learned Additional Attorney- General submitted that the process of approval was followed in accordance with the provisions of the Rules of Business of the government and the approval has been given after due consideration of the papers and documents submitted to the government, which includes a detailed project profile. It has been further submitted that there was no question of negligence and non-application of mind inasmuch as the process of the approval was initiated by a State executive and which was vetted by the Secretary of the Ministry of Shipping and then the same was placed before Hon'ble Prime Minister, who referred the same for scrutiny and consideration by the Council Committee on Economic Affairs, which consist of the Hon'ble Ministers and senior government officials, and the said committee after thorough examination and upon due consideration has approved the project proposal and then the Hon'ble Prime Minister has given the approval, and accordingly, the impugned letter of approval was issued and therefore it is absolutely incorrect to say that the impugned approval has been given arbitrarily without application of mind. The learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that, in fact, modification and amendments in the terms and conditions of the proposed agreement for implementation have been agreed upon after filing of the writ petition and those are beneficial for the country Referring to the contents of paragraph Nos. 22 to 30 of the writ petition it has been submitted that the writ petition has been filed malafide and with motive to stop implementation of the project, and now it is admitted that setting up of such container terminals are necessary for better economy of the country. The learned Additional Attorney-General referring to the letter written by the Assistant Private Secretary to Minister for Shipping dated 7-4-1997 (Annexure Z-5 to the Supplementary affidavit of the petitioner dated 31- 7-2002) submitted that by the said letter the government required the Overseas Trade Services to submit "technical and financial aspects of the project" but the same was not responded to. Then referring to the Annexure 2 of the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 1 it has been submitted that the Board of Investment has given their approval and registration to the project of the respondent No.8 by the said letter dated 14-1-1998 and according to the provisions of the Investment Board Act, 1989 any decision given by the Board of Investment in respect of a project or any industry shall be deemed as a decision given by the government. Referring to the summary dated 2-2- 1998 placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minister, the learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that in approving the said approval the registration given by the Board of Investment has been taken into consideration. It has been submitted that section 3 of the Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1980 authorises the government to sanction any Establishment with Foreign Capital and that section 3 of the Investment Board Act, 1989 contains that the provisions of the said Act and the Rules made there under shall have effect, notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law for the time being in force. One of the functions of the Board of Investment is to approve and register industrial projects in the private sector involving local and foreign capital and that any decision given by the Board of Investment under section 11(5) of the Investment Board Act is to be treated as a decision given by the government or by such other person or authority as is authorised by or entitled to give such decision, under the provisions of the relevant law on the relevant subject and such decision shall be implemented accordingly and that said sub-section 5 relates to facilities and services required for implementation of any project approved by the Board of Investment. The learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that the objection raised as to the location of the project is a matter to be decided by the government alone under its executive authority and as per policy decision and that the location for the proposed terminal at Patenga was decided earlier as far back as 1995. As is evidenced from the Master Plan of the Chittagong Port Authority (Annexure 10 to the Affidavit in- opposition of respondent No.1) and therefore it cannot be said that the location of the proposed project container port terminal at Patenga is against the public interest or has been made to benefit the respondent No.8. Lastly, it has been submitted that there is no malafide or arbitrariness or unreasonableness or discrimination and or negligence on the part of the government officials involved in the process of the impugned approval and the approval given by the government is bonafide and in the interest of the country and that further negotiation is being carried on for deriving more benefit for the country. 

 12. Mr. Rafiq-ul-Hoq, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.8, submitted that the submissions made by the learned Additional Attorney-General, have covered almost all the points in issue and he will not repeat the same and accordingly, adopted the same. However, Mr.Hoq, submitted that now it has been admitted that the project is a necessity for better economy of the country and that early implementation of the project will benefit the country economically and that the main objection raised was against the implementation of the project under BOO basis but, as has been confirmed by the learned Additional Attorney-General, now the project will be set up not under BOO basis but under BOT basis and accordingly, terms and conditions in the proposed agreement of implementation have been agreed to be amended and modified, and therefore, the Rule may be disposed of with observations and direction for early implementation of the project. The terms and conditions of the agreement for implementation are required to be finalised after going through the processes as enumerated in the supplementary affidavit dated 22-7-2002 of the respondent No. 1 which are (i) scrutiny by the Ministry of Law, and then (ii) further scrutiny by the Council Committee on Economic Affairs. It has been submitted that, in fact, the letter of approval dated 28-4-1998 is the "Letter of intention" to consider the proposal of the respondent No. 8 for setting up Container Port Terminals, on the terms and conditions to be agreed upon and therefore, the writ petition may be disposed of being pre-mature. 

 13. Dr. Kamal Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, referring to Annexure 2 of the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 1 dated 14-1-1998 submitted that it has been mentioned therein that the application of the respondent No.8 for registration was received on 13-1-1998 by the Board of Investment and by the said Annexure 2 dated 14-1-1998 the project of the respondent No.8 was given the registration and that shows the non-application of mind by the Board of Investment in according the registration inasmuch as the registration was given in haste, within one (1) day. The learned Advocate further submitted that the said registration was given by the Board of Investment without due consideration and arbitrarily in the absence of necessary papers and document namely, feasibility report or the project profile and the financial analysis showing benefit of the respondent No.1. Mr.Rafiqul-Hoq, the learned Advocate, appearing for the respondent No.8, in reply thereto submitted that the date 13-1-1998, as appearing, in the aforesaid Annexure 2 is not correct and that, in fact, the date 13-1-1998 as appearing is the date of the meeting in which the Board of Investment took resolution for giving registration to the project of the respondent No.8 and that actually the application of the respondent No.8 was received by the Board of Investment on 18-12-1997 and not on 13-1-1998. The learned Advocate further submitted that the registration was given considering the required information’s supplied through duly filling up the prescribed application form, procured from Board of Investment, which was processed by the Board of Investment after deposit of prescribed fees. The learned Advocate also submitted that, in fact, it was known to all that the SSA, USA is the real party, who approached the government for setting up of the container terminals and, as such, it is incorrect to say that through false representation the impugned approval has been obtained in the name of the respondent No.8, and that subsequently it has been found that some of the terms and conditions of the proposed agreement of implementation are against the interest of the beneficiary Bangladesh, hence necessary amendments by way of modification and amendments of such terms and conditions and or parts thereof in the agreement are being made to benefit the country and such exercise is continuing and will continue till finality is reached and that, if necessary, this Court being competent may also give directions to incorporate specific terms and conditions in the agreement in the interest of the country and in support of his contentions the learned Advocate referred to the decision in the case of Ms Sheha Zia vs WAPDA reported in PLD 1994 (SC) 693, wherein the Court gave some directions. 

 14. Dr. Kamal Hossain, the learned Advocate, also submitted as to the vulnerability of proposed location of the project and in reply to which Mr. Rafiq-ul-Hoq submitted that the Chittagong Port Authority as well as the Government as far back in 1996 have selected the present location for setting up of such project and that too also under BOO (Build, operate and own) basis and therefore the question of vulnerability now does not arise and such decision is to be taken by the government or the authority concerned Mr. Rafiq-ul-Hoq further submitted that since approval was given in 1998 and the respondent No.8 has undertaken several studies and ground-works required for early implementation of the project and has in the meantime invested over millions in Takas and in foreign currency and now is ready for entering into a formal contract for implementation of the project and the delay is causing continuous monetary loss, as such, in the greater interest of the country as well as of the respondent No.8, the project implementation process should not be stopped, more so when the respondent No. 8 has in the meantime accepted the terms and conditions of the Government of Bangladesh including the change made in the basic structure of the project from BOO basis to BOT basis. 

 The impugned approval has been communicated by the letter dated 28.4-1998, evidenced by Annexure J to the writ petition, copy of which has also been annexed as Annexure 5 to affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No.1, which contains that in response to the application of the respondent No.8 dated 29-12-1997 (wrongly mentioned as 29-12-1998) the government has considered and approved the proposal of the respondent No. 8 for establishment of two private sector Container Port Terminals, one at Patenga, Chittagong and one at Pangaon, Dhaka, under BOO (Build Own and Operate) basis and the integrated operation of barge service; and the respondent No.8 was further requested to take necessary steps for immediate implementation of the aforesaid integrated project. 

 16. It has been alleged by the writ petitioners that the said approval has been given arbitrarily and without application of mind and is against the public interest and through false representation, in describing the respondent No.8 as a Joint Venture of Bangladesh and USA companies, the impugned approval has been obtained; and that, in fact, the respondent No. 8 company was incorporated as a Joint Venture Company of a Bangladeshi Company and a Netherlands Company, as its only two share- holders; and that from the application of the respondent No.8 containing the proposal dated 29-12-1997 (copy annexed as Annexure 1 to the writ petition and as Annexure VIII to the affidavit-in- opposition of respondent No.8) and the summary dated 2-2-1998 prepared for the approval of the Hon'ble Prime Minister (Annexure 3 to the Affidavit-in-opposition of respondent No.1) show that the impugned approval was given in favour of the respondent No.8 treating it as a Joint Venture Company of Bangladesh and USA and that the government officials concerned acted negligently in not scrutinising the status and background of the respondent No. 8 company as well as those of the two shareholders, prior to preparing notes in the file and the summary dated 2-2-1998 for the approval of the Hon'ble Prime Minister. It has been alleged that the notices in the government file and the summary prepared for the Hon'ble Prime Minster were not based on evaluation of any project profile and/or financial analysis of the project and that there was no paper or document available in the government file showing any detail of the project and or the investments to be made and the expected earnings from the said proposed project and or the profit and loss account showing the expected amount that the government may earn annually from the project. In reply, the learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that in the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. I, it has been stated that the approval was given following the Rules of business and after examining the details of the project, which includes the feasibility study report and that the respondent No.8 submitted all necessary papers in 2 volumes, one under the caption "SSA Bangladesh Ltd, Corporate Literature December, 1997" and the other under caption "SSA Bangladesh Ltd Executive Business Plan December, 1997" along with the application dated 27-12-1997 and that the same were, duly examined and considered not only by the government officials 'but also by the Council Committee on Economic Affairs, consisting of some of the Hon'ble Members of the Cabinet and some senior government officials. 

 17. In order to appreciate the allegations and the reply thereto mentioned above we required the Additional Attorney-General to produce before us the relevant government file with original papers, through which the office note for approval of the proposal of the respondent No.8 was initiated, and it appeared from the note No. 1 dated 20-1-1998 in the file that a proposal dated 29-12-1997 along with papers in two (2) volumes namely, "Executive Business Plan December, 1997" and "Corporate Literature December, 1997" were submitted by the respondent No.8 company and subsequently a copy of the letter dated 14-1-1998 issued by the Board of Investment communicating the order granting registration number in favour of the respondent No. 8 was submitted and those papers were considered by the authority and on the basis of the aforesaid papers only the summary dated 2-2-1998 for consideration of the Hon'ble Prime Minister was prepared and that an initial "draft summary" was prepared and placed before the Secretary of the Ministry of Shipping, who required further improvement in the said summary by his note dated 21-1-1998 and thereafter, the amended "draft summary" prepared for the Hon'ble Prime Minster was placed before the Hon'ble Minister in charge of Shipping, who endorsed the same on 26-1-1998 and thereafter, the said summary, as amended, as it appears from the note of the Secretary dated 1-2-1998, was placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minster, who on perusal of the aforesaid summary on 19-2-1998 ordered for taking steps as per Rules and for placement of the same before the Council Committee on Economic Affairs for taking steps urgently (photo copy of the said summary containing order dated 19-2-1998 has been annexed as Annexure 3 to the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No.1). It appears from note No. 11 dated 27-4-1998 in the government file that the government approved the proposal of respondent No.8 considering the respondent No.8 as a Joint Venture Company of Bangladesh-USA and accordingly, the approval letter was issued on 28-4-1998 in the name of the respondent No.8. The application of the respondent No.8 dated 29-12-1997 was in the form of a letter, as available in the file of the government, and the same contains endorsement to show that the application of respondent No. 8 was received by the Ministry on 29-12-1997 and that subsequently on 15-1-1998 the respondent No.8 Company submitted a photo copy of the letter dated 14-1-1998 of the Board of Investment containing the registration number with which a copy of the duly filled up "prescribed form," containing the information’s furnished by the respondent No.8, including a list of Machinery and the nationality with the mailing address of the shareholders, was annexed. We have also perused the papers contained in the two volumes namely, (i) "SSA Bangladesh Ltd Executive Business Plan" and (ii) "SSA Bangladesh Ltd, Corporate Literature", submitted by the respondent No.8. "The SSA Bangladesh Ltd Corporate Literature" volume contains the information regarding various projects undertaken by Stevedoring Services of America of USA and the "SSA Bangladesh Ltd Executive Business Plan" volume contains papers showing the description, capability and background of the Stevedoring Services of America of USA and projection of the proposed Port Terminals. No project profile and or any feasibility report was available in the government file or in the aforesaid two volumes. On our query the learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that all papers are in the file and the aforesaid two (2) volumes and the papers therein have been considered by the officials while preparing the notes in the file and the summary dated 2-2-1998 for obtaining approval by the Hon'ble Prime Minister. Mr. Mohsin Rashid, the learned Advocate, who appeared with Mr. Rafiq-Ul- Hoq, also could not show us any feasibility report or any financial analysis of the project for our perusal from the records and the government file. 

 18. It is to be presumed that all actions taken by the government officials are in accordance with law and in the public interest and if any action of the government official is challenged, the challenger is required to prove such allegations. In the instant case it appears from the materials on record that in giving approval the authorities concerned have followed the Rules of Business, in that an application was received by the government and then a file was initiated with note and the note was placed before the concerned Secretary, who endorsed the note with his comments and then a draft summary was prepared for obtaining required approval from the Hon'ble Prime Minister and the said draft summary was examined and approved by the Hon'ble Minister of Shipping and then placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minister for approval and thereafter the Hon'ble Prime Minister in her wisdom ordered to take steps as per Rules and for placement of the summary before the Council Committee on Economic Affairs for consideration and recommendation and then with such recommendation of the Council Committee a summary was placed before the Hon'ble Prime Minister for approval and accordingly, approval was given by the Hon'ble Prime Minister and thereafter the letter of approval was issued by the Ministry of Shipping in favour of the respondent No.8. 

 19. The writ petitioners, as it appears, have challenged the process in which the approval has been given alleging, amongst others, that without obtaining required information regarding the project and relying on misrepresentation of the respondent No.8 as to its identity, the impugned approval was given and that the officials concerned were negligent in their duty, who did not examine the status or capability of the respondent No. 8 for implementation of the project. As found earlier that the respondent No.8 was incorporated as a private company under the Companies Act, 1994 with 2 shareholders namely, Orient Maritime Ltd and SSA Netherlands BV and in the copy of the Articles of Association of the respondent No. 8 company, annexed as Annexure H-1 to the writ petition, it is mentioned that the Orient Maritime Ltd is a Bangladeshi Company and SSA Netherlands BV is a Netherland Company and thus the Joint Venture Company was a Netherlands Bangladesh Company, yet in the application dated 29-12-1997 the respondent No. 8 Company described itself as a newly formed Joint Venture Company with the Stevedoring Services of USA ofthe United States of America and Orient Maritime Ltd of Bangladesh and that in the summary prepared for and placed before the Prime Minister, copy of which has been annexed as Annexure 3 to the affidavit-in- opposition of the respondent No.1, for obtaining the impugned approval, the respondent No.8 company has been fraudulently shown and described as a USA-Bangladesh Joint Venture Compare Levant portion of the summary dated 2-2-1998 is re- produced hereinbelow: 

 21. On scrutiny of the aforesaid file, which contains the notes, papers and documents relating to impugned approval we could not find any paper or legal document to show that the Stevedoring Services of America of USA has any connection with the respondent No.8 company and/or with the SSA Netherlands BV, the foreign share holder of the respondent No. 8 company. No note or paper or document was available in the file to confirm the identity or the status of SSA Netherlands BV. It appears that no query or attempt was made to get any information regarding the status and identity of SSA Netherlands BV. No paper or financial analysis or break-up as to the estimated profit and loss account on yearly basis of the proposed project showing the expected profit amount payable to Bangladesh was available in the file or in the said two volumes. There was neither any project profile or viability report of the proposed project nor any paper/document showing financial soundness, experience and capability of the SSA Netherlands BV to justify being a partner in the Joint Venture Company for setting up the proposed container terminals in Bangladesh was available in the file. In the absence of aforesaid information no person of prudence will normally take any step to consider any such project proposal. Thus it appears that the process of the impugned approval was initiated without application of mind and negligently. The letter dated 29-12-1997, as it appears, could at best be treated as a letter showing interest and in reply to which the Ministry of Shipping ought to have asked the respondent No. 8 to submit a detailed project proposal with financial analysis formally, which the Ministry has done in the case of overseas Trade Services, as evidenced by Annexure Z-6 to the affidavit-in-reply dated 31-7-2002. 

 22. We are surprised to note that the government officials treated the application dated 29-12-1997 as a project proposal in spite of the fact that the application was not accompanied with any project profile, feasibility/viability report on proposed project showing the financial analysis in respect of the investments/expenditures detailing the major heads of accounts, particularly the expenses to be incurred for construction of the. covered area and uncovered area and showing the expected income from the project on completion thereof and the amount, out of the expected income from the project, to be paid to the government of Bangladesh. Without knowing about the financial benefits to be received by the government, it cannot be said that the concerned government officers acted fairly and reasonably or prudently in considering the proposal of the respondent No, 8 and initiating a file for approval of such inadequate and incomplete offer. 

 24. It is now well settled that the State property may be in the form of legal right and in the nature of privilege. The government largesse known as privileges is now regarded as rights and the government cannot enter into any agreement in respect of its largesse arbitrarily or at its absolute discretion and it is also in the practice that in the event of allowing any such right, the normal procedure is to call for competitive bids to get a better price and to show fairness on the part of the authority. In the instant case, in view of the availability of the parties interested in setting up of container terminals, at least during the relevant period, the authority ought to have gone for competitive bids, more so when no specific amount of the expected money was mentioned in the letter of the respondent No.8 dated 29-12-1997, which Bangladesh would get from the earning by the proposed project. This indicates arbitrariness on the part of the government officials involved in processing the file and notes for the impugned approval. The government officials involved in the process of the impugned approval thus appears to have acted not only negligently but also acted arbitrarily for the benefit of a private party, and against the public interest. From the records available it appears that the authority was aware that even when a proposal is pending for consideration, further competitive bids required to be invited under the "Swiss challenge" scheme to see if better offer could be available and to make the deal fair and reasonable, yet they preferred not to go for the same on the plea of delay, which plea in the facts and circumstances appears to us to be not bonafide and therefore the actions of the officials concerned are unfair, unreasonable and discriminatory. 

 25. Apart from this we have found that the respondent No. 8 company has been registered illegally as a company, since formed with one legal share holder only inasmuch as the foreign share holder of the Joint Venture Company, namely, SS Netherlands BV was none-existent in the eye of law on the date respondent No.8. Company was incorporated i.e. on 15-12-1997, and the allotments of shares in favour of SSA Netherlands BV were made illegally, since not in existence and therefore, the registration of the project of the illegally formed respondent No. 8 company by the Board of Investment is void and accordingly, the approval of the proposed project in favour of the respondent No. 8 is void ab initio and consequently, the subsequent process and or actions based on the void approval of the proposal are illegal and without lawful authority. 

 28. The project of container terminals is within the jurisdiction of the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) under the CPA Ordinance, 1976 and it appears that prior to giving the registration the Board of Investment authority did not consult the Chittagong Port Authority. The registration of the proposed project of the respondent No.8, as approved by the Board of investment in the absence of any feasibility report and financial analysis is thus an act of negligence and arbitrariness. The allegation of non-application of mind against the Board of Investment has its basis since it did not enquire about the status, financial background and expense and the capability of the respondent No. 8 as well.as those of its shareholders, to implement such a project of national importance, Thus the allegations as to non-application of mind, negligence and arbitrariness on the part of the officials and the members of the Board of Investment involved in the process of approval and giving registration to the proposed project of the respondent No.8 are established. 

 29. It is unusual that an approval to a proposal is given first and then the terms and conditions thereof are being settled in between the parties. The impugned approval is such an unusual case. It has been submitted that the impugned approval letter may be treated as a letter of intention. But having regard to the fact that on the basis of the impugned approval letter some leases of lands have already been made final in favour of the respondent No. 8 and directions have been given by the Ministry of Shipping for leasing out further lands during the pendency of finalisation of the terms and conditions of the proposed agreement for implementation. It has also been submitted that the scheme of the project under BOO (Build Operate and Own) basis has been decided to be changed to BOT (Build Operate and Transfer) basis. On our asking the learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that although in the drafts of the terms and conditions of the proposed "Agreement for Implementation" it has been decided that the project will be implemented on BOT basis instead of BOO basis, as approved, but no formal order has been passed to that effect and, as such, the impugned letter of approval dated 28-4-1998 containing the implementation of the project under BOO basis still stands. It has been submitted on behalf of the petitioners that they have actually challenged the process in which the impugned approval was given and that unless an agreement comes into existence lawfully, that cannot be challenged. Till date there is no existence of any agreement and, according to the contesting respondents, the process is still going on to finalise the agreement. In view of the principle laid down in the case of Kazi Moklesur Rahman, reported in 26 DLR (SC) 44 unless an agreement reaches its finality, the same cannot be challenged. In the aforesaid case a treaty was signed in between the heads of the governments of Bangladesh and India, known as Delhi Treaty, 1974, and it was to become effective only on ratification by the Parliaments of the respective countries but prior to such ratification the said Delhi Treaty was challenged in Court and accordingly, the challenge was found to be pre-mature. Since we have seen that the impugned approval has been given effect, even in the absence of the agreement of implementation, which is under process, and based on such approval leases of land are given in favour of respondent No. 8, the impugned approval appears to be an independent form of a full-fledged contract, which has been processed arbitrarily without application of mind with negligence in favour of an illegal company, and therefore, the approval is illegal, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and accordingly, the subsequent actions taken and orders passed based on the aforesaid impugned approval are also without lawful authority and illegal. 

 33. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned Additional Attorney-General that the government and the respondent No.8 company have agreed to change the basic structure of the impugned approval for the proposed project from the BOO scheme to BOT scheme, with 30 years period, apart from other changes agreed to be made in the terms and conditions in the proposed agreement of implementations, after the instant writ action has been initiated and aforesaid changes are admittedly beneficial for the country and such submission having not been contradicted by the contesting respondent No.8, and in view of our discussions made hereinabove the question of locus standi of the petitioners and the maintainability of the writ petition have become academic and goes in favour of the petitioners. 

 34. In the report of the committee of six( 6) Secretaries dated 30-4-2002, copy of which has been annexed as Annexure 27 to the Supplementary Affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent· No. 1 dated 27-2-2002, and in particular clause 3.16 at running page 33 thereof, it appears that for implementation of project 63 months is required and the period would start after the agreement for implementation is signed and executed and also in view of the fact that through invitation of competitive bids better offers may be received within a reasonable period, say three (3) months, and thus the period of implementation of the project will be 66 months in place of proposed 63 months, which will be of no consequence for the instant project. The committee of six (6) Secretaries in their report dated 30-4-2002 in clauses 3.4, 3.5 and 3.6 have advocated for not to go for open bids or to adopt method of Swiss Challenge on the ground of delay, which appears to us not to be bonafide. Even in the summary placed before the present Hon'ble Prime Minister (who took oath in October, 2001) it has been mentioned that the respondent No. 8 company is a Joint Venture Company of USA and Bangladesh, the copy of the summary dated 4-5-2002 has been annexed as Annexure 29 to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No.1 dated 22-7-2002 and that, probably, might have misled the Hon'ble Prime Minister in giving her approval for negotiation with respondent No.8, treating SSA USA as a shareholder of the Company. It appears from the contents of the drafts of the "Agreement for Implementation" dated 5-3- 2001 and 22-5-2002 that some quarter has been trying to avoid the process of competitive bids for the project. It also appears from the notes, papers and the materials placed before us that efforts were/are being made to favour respondent No.8 although unfairly and against interest of the country. 

 37. Since we are of the opinion that the impugned approval of the project in favour of the respondent No. 8 by the government is illegal and without lawful authority, the subsequent actions on the basis of the said impugned approval are also illegal, and thus the Rule is decided. We therefore, refrain from making any comment on the submissions made by the learned Advocates of the contesting parties hereof relating to the vulnerability of the proposed location of the project and whether the proposed location should be allotted to any foreigner for setting up and managing any such port terminal and all other allegations made in writ petition, since not necessary at this stage. 

 39. Considering the process adopted for giving approval to the project of respondent No.8 and the negligence on the part of the officials and the persons involved, on the face of the record, as discussed above and the tendency to avoid the process of competitive bids, we are of the view that an investigation need be made to look into the matter in depth whether the officials and persons involved in the process have tried and are trying to avoid the competitive bid process and acted in favour of a private party against the interest of the country and mislead the successive Hon'ble Prime Ministers in obtaining their respective approvals showing Stevedoring Services of America USA as a shareholder of respondent No.8 company. 

 40. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned approval to the project of the respondent No. 8 communicated by the letter dated 28-4-1998, evidenced by Annexure J to the writ petition, is declared to be illegal, without lawful authority and of no legal effect and accordingly, all actions taken on the basis of the impugned approval are declared to be illegal, without lawful authority and of no legal effect.
